speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It is through such difficult times that we prove our mettle as a nation and as a people.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Government's response to the crisis has been swift.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Various Ministries have detailed how they are introducing measures to mitigate the impact to their respective sectors.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It has been a defining element in the Budget 2020 debate.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The fact that this Government has sufficient financial resources, accumulated through financial prudence, was not lost on the Members.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Neither was the call for all segments of the society to play an active part as Team Singapore in riding out the challenge.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Indeed, many stakeholders came together to deliver help.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The COVID-19 outbreak may have generated fear and anxiety among Singaporeans but it has also shown our community at its best.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have heard about the numerous ground-up, spontaneous acts of care.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa shared how larger businesses are stepping up to help smaller ones tide through this crisis, while the SG Cares Volunteer Centres brought community groups and resourceful corporations along to reach out to vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These efforts exemplify the strong community spirit in Singapore today.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Dr Koh Poh Koon and Mr Teo Ser Luck rightly pointed out that in times of crisis, come opportunity.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Some Members, such as Prof Yaacob Ibrahim, have called for Singapore to take stock and reflect on how we can be better versions of ourselves as a response to the challenge.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Many of our industries and businesses appreciate the need to transform so they are better prepared to deal with the next disruption.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Members like Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap and Miss Cheng Li Hui asked that we also build up Singapore's civic spirit, psychological defence and social cohesion so that we emerge from this crisis stronger as a nation.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Even as we are occupied with the challenges of the present, we have our eyes firmly on the long-term issues.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Many Members spoke passionately on ensuring Singapore's competitiveness and relevance in a fast-changing world.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Lim Swee Say reminded us that our common goal is to generate sufficient resources to improve the lives of all our people.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is evidenced by the large number of questions received by MOE and MOM on education and training for Singaporeans, pipping even MOH despite the current public health situation.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore's current and future challenges will be increasingly complex and unexpected.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: If we harness the diverse strengths of Singaporeans and work together as one, just as we are doing with COVID-19, we can turn our challenges into opportunities, our problems into possibilities.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We can build a future Singapore that we and those after us can be proud of.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The debates in the past few days have presented us with long-term challenges – how to age well, how to uplift the disadvantaged, how to build a climate resilient nation and so on.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To tackle them, we must partner to build our Singapore together.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: So, I am heartened to hear the theme of partnerships come through strongly in our debates.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singaporeans can and want to play a bigger role in shaping Singapore.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Government agencies will be opening up many more opportunities for Singaporeans from all walks of life and all segments of the society.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will co-create and co-deliver initiatives to make Singapore a resilient nation, a city of possibilities, a society with opportunities for all and a caring and cohesive community.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: First, a resilient nation in the face of global disruptions.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Members agree that it is critical we remain nimble.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Cedric Foo and Mr Ong Teng Koon spoke about the opportunities and challenges caused by the rise of the digital economy.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To this end, MCI shared how its community partners are helping Singaporeans and our SMEs build digital skills.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Dennis Tan and Er Dr Lee Bee Wah highlighted the dangers of climate change.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And might I say, the youths are also very passionate about this aspect.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore should continue to be an attractive place to live, work and play.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Douglas Foo and Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar highlighted more can be done to ensure Singaporeans' continued employability and relevance for the future.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Zainal Sapari spoke passionately on harnessing the resources of our mid-career workers – those in their 40s and 50s.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As Ms Denise Phua put it, our social challenges need to be tackled together, and the community's role is crucial in ensuring no one falls through the cracks.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In light of growing polarisation around the world, we need to show regard and respect for one another regardless of our differences and build a cohesive community with a shared identity.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Government will work with Singaporeans on this journey.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: On behalf of the House, I would also like to thank you, Mr Speaker, and your deputies for your able stewardship of the debate proceedings.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I also thank the Parliament Secretariat and staff for their dedicated assistance and responses to our requests and queries, particularly those who took our temperatures and kept our premises clean, and the interpreters who were with us every step of this debate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: A year ago, we had an extensive conversation about cows, and a particular sacred cow, to be precise.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We debated till the cows came home, we milked the issue to death and we slayed the creature good and proper.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You would have thought that, that was done.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I do not know if you have noticed but the cow is back again this year.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This time, it is called "Impossible Meat" – and we even sampled it in the form of satay and gyoza, which was really quite delicious.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We had the whole Mandai Zoo, River Safari and Jurong Bird Park here as well.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But could all these be our future source of protein?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: MEWR then talked about mosquitoes with names like Aedes mosquitoes and Wolbachia as we are reminded to stay vigilant in our war against dengue.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Then, came the cats, and the pet birds and dogs during MND's Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And then, MOT came on board as well, addressed the concerns about the Raffles Banded Langurs – not just any monkeys but Langurs named Leonardo, Michelangelo, Donatello and Raphael.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, in an indirect way, turtles of the Ninja genus were also dragged into the conversation as well.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: All these creatures were raised not for any trivial reasons.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some revolved around our survival in a time of possible food disruption.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some were about disease management and its sometimes fatal impact on our people.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some were discussed in terms of our common space with pets and how we treat animals in our society.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And some were discussed in the context of how we must try to be sensitive to our environment and nature, amidst development.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Langurs may not mean very much to many Singaporeans – perhaps it should – but it means a great deal to Dr Andie Ang and her team who are working closely with LTA on the local habitat concerned.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: All these are just small slivers of a bigger whole.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So very much goes on without many of us realising it.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think an opportunity to debate and discuss this in Parliament reminds us of how much goes on out there, every day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Nothing is too trivial not to be addressed.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: My Deputy Speakers and I had the privilege of enduring all your speeches in the last few weeks.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I make no apologies for the use of that term.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Because it can be substantive and heavy; and it represents an even larger body of work that exists out there in the Ministries and agencies as they seek to make life better for all of us.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: People often ask me to view this video clip or other from other parliaments.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some are the fighting ones which are very exciting.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You can go and watch it but do not get ideas.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Others are most eloquent, humorous, sharply satirical – impressive.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But I then ask myself, after watching then, "So, therefore... and what is next?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, what then do we do?" Words can flow like honey, music to the ears but they must be real.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They set in motion the journey from words to deeds.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For that to happen, we need processes, specific initiatives, mechanisms, effective delivery for good to take place.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is really quite some distance to travel from ideas and rhetoric to reality.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Today, we are often seized by form and style.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But how to get things done way less exciting, much less glamorous.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, it is challenging to sit through all these, but it is the least we can do to honour the effort and hard work put in by so many.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Budget is the blueprint from which we build our future.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: To be honest, many do not actually watch the clips of every speaker here, read their speeches and the responses but we are definitely very quick to comment!

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, do give it a shot because they can be quite educational and give us a sense of how we intend to address the concerns that are out there.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They also show us how we can realise our vision of the kind of Singapore we want to build together.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is true, perhaps we could do with a little more flair, a little more panache but never, never give up the way we do business here in Singapore – solid, down-to-earth ideas, plans and execution.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And not just creating beautiful castles in the air.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We read of some Singaporeans shunning our nurses.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Rather than cheering them on and honouring them as many have done, these Singaporeans are concerned about themselves.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Why is there a rush for masks or groceries or toilet paper?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In many countries and we read of this today, this is severely affecting the frontline healthcare workers who face problems being properly equipped.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ultimately, our individual actions affect society and it comes back round.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can we, in Singapore, rise above ourselves and be different from others?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As Leader said, can we be better versions of ourselves?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In our annual Budget as well, do we not also grapple with the individual and society?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If we, as a people, are prepared to think about the collective and the future, we can sit down, we can discuss business and talk about what to do.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But if it is just about me and myself, today and now, then, honestly there would not be much of a Singapore or future to aspire towards.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: From the COVID-19 situation, we also realise how inter-connected we are, both within Singapore and also with the world.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are part of a common humanity and we cannot turn our backs on that.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You can see how easy it is to infect each other.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You can see how easy it is to blame each other.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But are we also not sometimes guilty here in Singapore as we blame others as well?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But do we not also realise that in other people's eyes, we are "the others"?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sadly, we read recently of one of our young Singaporeans being beaten up by YOBS in England simply because he is Asian, because he is Chinese.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There is the good that comes with globalisation but there are also disamenities and we know that.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some politicians use it to stir a visceral anger that comes from the nationalism that is within all of us.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sometimes, it will be about race and religion.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We see it in our discourse here in Singapore sometimes.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We need to remain plugged in so that Singaporeans can benefit.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We maximise the positive outcomes while mitigating the negatives.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And our team is still learning and adjusting, even as we speak, and the real payoffs are in the lives saved.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have also been doing so for food for the longest time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: When we spend for the future, in any Budgets, we have less to spend on the present.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: No average person is seized by these long-term issues that may or may not happen and we all know the common complaint that Singaporeans may have: why do you not care for me today?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But you see, the truth is we do.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: That is why we are able to do what we do during this crisis.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We did the same in all the major crises that came by our way in the past.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The economic impact will affect more people detrimentally than those who may be infected.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: That is why we pay attention to the economy, we budget for the present, but we continue to budget for future uncertainties as well.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think many countries are guilty of that.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Imagine if we decided to spend more, save less.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is far easier to be popular than to be prepared.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But I am grateful to this Parliament, to all of us here, both Government and Opposition, for supporting these moves.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: When you look past all the political bluster, there is actually strong unity in approach, not only for this Budget, but for the Budgets past.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Parliament is able to do this only because the people of Singapore are prepared to support it.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Yet, I know every one of us will still grumble about why we did not get more of this or did not get more of that.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But our people's support allows Parliament to have the courage to take the more difficult but yet perhaps the more correct path.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This support will not exist and does not exist if there is no sense of unity and no sense of togetherness, which is why the idea of Singapore Together is really, really, so precious.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is not just a slogan, something that we just mouth off in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: They are actually things that we can do.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: SG Cares, for example, helps us to reach out, volunteer, connect with others.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It allows us to practise our empathy and compassion and to bring out the innate good that is in all of us.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Our community efforts on the ground bring neighbours together to forge bonds that can bind.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Our emphasis on family seeks to help strengthen family bonds because that is where it all starts.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Even our NS journey allows many to come together despite the differences in backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It now leaves me to thank all Singaporeans – everyone here, those at the frontline, all those behind the scenes – who made this all possible.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Passing Budget 2020 is only the first step.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Let us go forth and translate these words into deeds.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Because this is what our Democracy is all about.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Because this is Singapore and because we are Singapore.
